items.fact: RMSNorm (2019 onward): y = x / RMS(x) * gamma, RMS = sqrt(mean x^2); LayerNorm without mean-centring and without beta

items.fact: Init: constant (naive) gives the symmetry problem, every neuron same input and gradient, cannot diversify

items.fact: Init: plain random breaks symmetry but scale critical; too small vanishes, too large explodes
items.where: Reading section 7 table row 2; calculator

items.fact: Xavier: Var = 2/(n_in + n_out); uniform and normal flavours; for sigmoid/tanh, roughly linear and zero-mean near 0
items.where: Reading section 7 table and derivation (Eq. 16 uniform bound)

items.fact: He: Xavier modified for ReLU, variance doubled to 2/n_in because ReLU zeroes half the activations (non-zero mean); ReLU-family default
items.where: Reading section 7 table and derivation; calculator; measured 0.990 per layer

items.fact: LeCun: Var = 1/n_in, pairs with SELU
items.where: Reading section 7 table; LeCun 1998 and Klambauer 2017 cited

items.fact: All variance-scaling schemes keep activation and gradient variance roughly constant across layers, preventing vanishing/exploding gradients from step one
